title: Seeing Through Deception: Uncovering Misleading Creator Intent in Multimodal News with Vision-Language Models

model.params_source: paper Appendix D.1 (temperature 0, single run); o4-mini ignores temperature/top_p, reasoning_effort not stated (API default medium assumed); max_completion_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: text-modified instances {I, T', A}: M-Sub (Text) 2,000, M-Sig (Text) 2,000 and NM 2,000
task.approximation: Reasoning effort unstated; the NM class is shared between the text and image splits (assumed the same 2,000 originals).

items.source: jiayingwu19/DeceptionDecoded (gated, auto-approval): deceptiondecoded.json, data.tar.gz (images), visualnews_data_mapping.json; code at https://github.com/jiayingwu19/DeceptionDecoded
items.config_or_split: text-modified subset (M-Sub Text, M-Sig Text, NM)

prompt.user_template:
{image}Your task is to determine whether a news piece has been intentionally distorted to mislead readers.
The news piece consists of an image with its caption: {caption}. You are also provided a trustworthy reference article related to the same event: {article}.
Follow the structured steps below and strictly adhere to the output format.
Important Note: Focus only on the content of the news piece. The use of AI tools to assist image creation does not, by itself, indicate distortion.
Answer the following questions:
Q1. Has the news piece been intentionally distorted by its creator to mislead readers, such that it conveys a biased, controversial, or manipulated message?
- Respond with one of the following: [Yes, No]. Then provide a brief explanation.
Q2. What is the source of the manipulation—text or image?
- If answer to Q1 is “Yes”, answer with one of the following: [Text, Image].
- If answer to Q1 is “No”, answer: “NA”.
Q3. What does the distortion suggest about the news publisher's intent?
- If answer to Q1 is “Yes” :
Primary Influence (Desire): Select up to three from the following list, ranked by relevance: [Political Polarization, Social Polarization, Cultural and Religious Polarization, Economic Misinformation, Public Health and Safety, Environmental and Scientific Polarization, Geopolitical and International Relations, Psychological and Emotional Manipulation].
- If answer to Q1 is “No”, respond with “NA” for Q3.
Output Format: Respond in the following exact JSON format, preserving the structure, punctuation, and delimiters. Do not add any extra line breaks or formatting outside this structure:
{ “pred”: “Answer to Q1, followed by a brief explanation”,
“source”: "Answer to Q2",
“desire”: "Answer to Q3" }

placeholders.image: the news image attached to the message
placeholders.caption: items.caption (original or modified)

prompt.verbatim: full (one extraction join 'thatit' split into 'that it')

output.parse: json field pred: leading Yes/No (regex ^\s*(Yes|No)) -> misleading / non-misleading
output.postprocess: strip; malformed JSON: first 'Yes'/'No' token after 'pred'; no match = incorrect

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: Text Avg.: unweighted mean of the per-class accuracies on M-Sub (Text), M-Sig (Text) (correct = Yes) and NM (correct = No), each over 2,000 instances.
metric.original_location: Table 2, row o4-mini / I, column Text Avg. (64.8 / 91.2 / 95.4 per class)

open_points: Gated Hugging Face dataset (jiayingwu19/DeceptionDecoded, ~2 GB image archive) must be accepted and downloaded by a human, and each call needs the news image attached; text-only messages cannot reproduce the {I, T', A} setting.
notes: Articles plus images make each call ~2k input tokens; o4-mini reasoning output adds cost. The paper's default paradigm is consistency-oriented (C); the claim uses the implication-oriented (I) row. || [hooks_2 2026-09-07] reviewed for a per-paper hook: gated data + image inputs; no hook written.
